program: Survivor safety, trauma support and economic empowerment
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Houston Area Women’s Center provides confidential support to survivors of domestic and sexual violence in Houston.
Its services include crisis response, supportive housing, counseling, advocacy and help navigating legal and social resources.
Economic empowerment and practical family support aim to make safety and recovery sustainable.
strengths: Current official reporting distinguishes counseling, housing placements and repeated hotline contacts.
Original returns and a consolidated audit make resource and affiliate boundaries inspectable.
Financial coaching, housing advocacy and practical support provide a resource mechanism beyond free retail counseling.
reservations: Nearly 2,700 counseling and advocacy clients include children and do not establish adult completed treatment.
Incremental symptom utility, safety and disposable resource gains remain unsupported priors.
Public assistance, partner services, capital expansion and marginal funding require further counterfactual work.

sections.what: Houston Area Women’s Center provides confidential support to survivors of domestic and sexual violence in Houston. Its services include crisis response, supportive housing, counseling, advocacy and help navigating legal and social resources. Economic empowerment and practical family support aim to make safety and recovery sustainable.
sections.monitoring: Official 2025 reporting gives nearly 2,700 women, men and children counseled or advocated for, 913 women, children and families housed, 134 longer-term housing placements and 35,446 calls. They may overlap; calls, apartment capacity and nights are not added as unique beneficiaries. Request annual adult household deduplication, actual counseling dose, safe housing persistence, privacy incidents, net earnings and usable assistance versus alternative supports. A search result annual report for Family Service League in New Jersey was rejected as the wrong recipient.
sections.qualitative: Current official reporting distinguishes counseling, housing placements and repeated hotline contacts. Original returns and a consolidated audit make resource and affiliate boundaries inspectable. Financial coaching, housing advocacy and practical support provide a resource mechanism beyond free retail counseling. Nearly 2,700 counseling and advocacy clients include children and do not establish adult completed treatment. Incremental symptom utility, safety and disposable resource gains remain unsupported priors. Public assistance, partner services, capital expansion and marginal funding require further counterfactual work. Original Form 990 confirms EIN 74-2029166 and current recipient identity. Recipient-owned giving route was read without a donation transaction. The audit consolidates HAWC ESH LLC; no separate affiliate grants are double counted.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $42.23 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 3.545801 clinical QALYs and 0.281596 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.002368 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $16,163,406. Nearly 2,700 mixed counseling/advocacy clients supply only an approximate annual reference. Judged .6 adult-household mapping and .3 additional annual response give 486 exposed households. The clinical subgroup is within that union: .2 meaningful symptom/safety improvement times .08 utility for .5 finite year; this is not an RCT-calibrated recipient effect or assumed mortality gain. Full one-off .0005 clinical harm per exposed household represents a weak privacy/safety deterioration prior. Independent .25 resource success receives $600 net additional work resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal, childcare, commute and displaced earnings, plus $400 usable assistance after alternative funding; each positive component receives overlap .5 before subtracting full $100 attendance, privacy-related process and foregone-pay burden. Successful households net $400; others lose $100. Union 486 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 97.2; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Assistance can transfer resources from taxpayers or displaced recipients rather than create social income. A distinct payer stress prices additional budget/displacement, not the same donation cost again. Provider stress covers genuinely external opportunity resources only. Central external incidence zero is unknown-neutral. Housing and child benefits outside this narrow adult household channel remain unknown, including associated burdens. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: Original FY2024 tax expense $16,076,053 plus $28,035 donated services removed from expense reconciliation and $59,318 netted event cost gives $16,163,406. FY2023 $14,814,054 plus $67,723 donated services and $54,181 event cost gives $14,935,958. FY2022 $17,276,637 plus $165,995 donated services and $30,242 event cost gives $17,472,874. The 2024 consolidated audit reports $16,116,236 including event cost, a different entity/reconciliation scope; tax-based full recognized recipient cost is used consistently, not that audit total plus intercompany costs. Current 2025 activity is paired with latest read 2024 original cost, explicitly a timing mismatch. Capital assets are not treated as a repeated annual expense. A later audit index lead was not used as verified current expense.

model.costScope: Full recognized recipient annual cost versus limited adult counseling/economic-support channel; capital and other portfolio outcomes/marginal gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Houston-area adult households; .98 local share judged, not verified patient residence
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Existing public victim compensation, shelter/counseling providers, housing grants, community employment support and family help retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional safety and reduced trauma burden plus usable household work/assistance resources, not hotline calls or housing nights
